note: Comparison-note paragraphs on Saints.Bible staging that quoted or described the pre-revision English, rewritten to match the revised readings.

changes.before_html: Both: leave Me so My anger destroys them, and I will make you a great nation; Latin adds 'wrath may blaze'.
changes.after_html: Both: let Me alone so My anger destroys them, and I will make you a great nation; Latin adds 'wrath may blaze'.
changes.reason: The Latin–English reading now says “Let Me alone”, not “Leave Me”.

changes.before_html: Repetition of the law / second law expresses the king’s written law text in related ways; Latin-English explicitly mentions receiving a model.
changes.after_html: Repetition of the law / second law expresses the king’s written law text in related ways; Latin-English explicitly mentions receiving a master copy.
changes.reason: The Latin–English reading now says “receiving a master copy”, not “receiving a model”.

changes.before_html: Different. Latin–English has “While these were being brought low through…”; Greek–English has “as a rebuke to”. This changes a local detail or emphasis in the displayed renderings; the complete wording and retained source notes delimit the judgment.
changes.after_html: Different. Latin–English has “While these were being brought low as a rebuke for…”; Greek–English has “as a rebuke to”. This changes a local detail or emphasis in the displayed renderings; the complete wording and retained source notes delimit the judgment.
changes.reason: The note quotes the old Latin–English wording “brought low through”; it now reads “brought low as a rebuke for”.

changes.before_html: The necessity of passing through Samaria agrees; the difference is English wording.
changes.after_html: The necessity of passing through Samaria agrees; the English renderings are identical apart from the capital in He.
changes.reason: Latin–English now reads “he had to pass through Samaria”, matching the other column, so no wording difference remains.

changes.before_html: Both: perpetual sacrifice at the tent entrance before the Lord; Latin 'where I will appoint to speak', Greek 'where I will make Myself known to speak'.
changes.after_html: Both: perpetual sacrifice at the tent entrance before the Lord; Latin 'where I will arrange to speak', Greek 'where I will make Myself known to speak'.
changes.reason: The note quoted the old Latin–English ‘appoint’; the reading now says ‘arrange’.

changes.before_html: Both break the bird open by its wings without dividing it and burn it on the altar wood as a fragrant offering.
changes.after_html: Latin breaks its wings and Greek breaks it open by its wings; both do so without dividing it and burn it on the altar wood as a fragrant offering.
changes.reason: The note said both break the bird ‘open’; the Latin–English reading now says only ‘break its wings’.

changes.before_html: Both let a kinsman redeem a poor brother's sold property; Latin says if the relative wishes it, Greek says the nearest kinsman shall ransom.
changes.after_html: Both let a kinsman redeem a poor brother's sold property; Latin says if the relative is willing, Greek says the nearest kinsman shall ransom.
changes.reason: The note paraphrased the old ‘wishes to do so’; the reading now says ‘is willing’.

changes.before_html: Both run the boundary from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt and end at the Great Sea.
changes.after_html: Both run the boundary from Azmon to the torrent (Greek: Wadi) of Egypt and end at the Great Sea.
changes.reason: The note gave ‘Wadi of Egypt’ for both columns; the Latin–English reading now says ‘torrent of Egypt’.

changes.before_html: Both: the law Moses commanded us, an inheritance of Jacob's assembly.
changes.after_html: Both: the law Moses commanded us, an inheritance of Jacob's multitude (Greek: assemblies).
changes.reason: The note gave ‘assembly’ for both columns; the Latin–English reading now says ‘multitude’.
